title: Nuh and the Destroyed Nations
question: Why does the Quran keep returning to nations that vanished?
intro: The Quran tells of Nuh and of nations whose ruins lay along routes the Prophet's ﷺ listeners travelled (37:137-138): 'Ad, the people of Hud; Thamud, the people of Salih; the people of Lut; and Madyan, the people of Shu'ayb. Idris is mentioned briefly, as a man of truth raised to a high station (19:56-57).

These stories are told again and again, often in nearly the same words. That is deliberate. The Quran is showing a pattern: a messenger from among the people calls them to worship Allah alone and to stop a specific wrong. The powerful refuse. Warnings and time are given. Then comes the outcome.
The Quran calls this sunnat Allah, Allah's unchanging way. It is told as a mirror, not a spectacle.

passages.context: Surah Nuh is Nuh's own report to Allah. 29:14 says he stayed among his people 950 years.
passages.point: He called them night and day, in public and in private. They put their fingers in their ears. The problem was never a lack of effort.
passages.label: stated

passages.context: During the Flood. When Nuh pleads for his son, Allah answers: "he is not of your family" (11:46).
passages.point: Even a prophet's son was not saved by kinship. Safety lay only in Allah's mercy, and faith is not inherited.
passages.label: stated

passages.context: Ash-Shu'ara gives Nuh, Hud, Salih, Lut and Shu'ayb the same opening words (26:106-109, 26:161-164).
passages.point: Each messenger asks his people to fear Allah, calls himself trustworthy, and asks no payment. One message, many nations.
passages.label: stated

passages.context: Follows brief accounts of Nuh, Ibrahim, Lut, Shu'ayb, 'Ad, Thamud, Qarun and Pharaoh (29:14-39).
passages.point: Each was seized for its own wrongdoing, by stones, a blast, the earth or the flood. Allah did not wrong them; they wronged themselves.
passages.label: stated

visual.title: The pattern of the destroyed nations
visual.caption: The same five stages repeat across the accounts. Each nation's wrong is different; the pattern is not, because "you will never find in the way of Allah any change" (35:43).

items.label: A messenger
items.text: "Their brother", one of their own, is sent.

items.label: The call
items.text: Worship Allah alone, and leave a specific wrong.

items.label: Elite rejection
items.text: The eminent call him a liar or in error.

items.label: Warning and respite
items.text: Signs, hardship and time to turn back.

items.label: The outcome
items.text: Believers saved; those who persist are seized.

examples.label: Nuh's people
examples.text: Centuries of refusal; taken by the Flood.

examples.label: 'Ad, with Hud
examples.text: Proud builders of fortresses; a violent wind.

examples.label: Thamud, with Salih
examples.text: Hamstrung the she-camel; seized by the shriek.

examples.label: Lut's people
examples.text: Indecency done openly; a rain of stones.

examples.label: Madyan, with Shu'ayb
examples.text: Cheating in measure and weight; seized by the shriek.

word.nuance: A sunnah is a well-trodden path, a way followed again and again. Here it means how Allah deals with nations: He does not destroy towns while their people set things right (11:117), and His way does not change (35:43). The same word names the Prophet's ﷺ way.

mixup.myth: These nations were destroyed suddenly, without warning or a chance to change.
mixup.truth: Each account shows long warning first. Nuh called his people for 950 years (29:14) and promised them forgiveness, rain and wealth if they turned back (71:10-12). Thamud were given three days (11:65). The Quran says Allah would not destroy towns unjustly while their people were reformers (11:117).

remember: Nuh, Hud, Salih, Lut and Shu'ayb brought the same core message to different peoples.
Each nation had its own wrong: arrogance, cruelty, indecency or cheating in trade.
Warning and time came first; the outcome followed their own choices (29:40).

quiz.q: How long did Nuh stay among his people, according to 29:14?
quiz.why: 29:14: "he remained among them a thousand years minus fifty years." Surah Nuh (71:5-9) shows how he used that time.

quiz.q: Which wrong did Shu'ayb especially warn Madyan against?
options: Building a sign on every height
quiz.why: 11:84-85: "do not decrease from the measure and the scale... give full measure and weight in justice." Building on every height was Hud's warning to 'Ad (26:128).

quiz.q: When Nuh's son refused to board, where did he say he would go?
quiz.why: 11:43: "I will take refuge on a mountain to protect me from the water." Nuh replied that there is no protector that day except for whom Allah gives mercy.

reflect: Nuh kept calling for centuries. Is there someone you stopped hoping for whom you could gently try again?
